description: simulate a construction file — resolve every named oligo and plasmid across the whole project folder, run the steps, report each product and its length, say whether a sequencing primer actually sits inside that product and has only one site, and with --maps compare each product with the map somebody recorded for it, up to rotation and reverse complement
phrases: does this PCR give the right product
does the sequencing primer anneal in the PCR product
is the sequencing oligo inside that pcr product
how big is the PCR product
does the simulated plasmid match the recorded map
compare what this builds with the plasmid map on file
is the map in the folder the thing this construction makes
check a primer for a second binding site

requires.note: parseCF and simCF — the simulator itself
resolves the named inputs across the project, including sequences that exist only inside a labsheet workbook
--maps: whether a simulated molecule and a recorded map are the same DNA, up to rotation and strand

returns: one line per product with its length in bp; the named inputs that resolved nowhere; any enzyme the simulator does not know; with --primes, where that oligo sits in each product and whether it binds more than once; and with --maps, match / differs (with the length delta and the first differing base) / no map for each product. Exit 1 when a step failed or a product differs from its map
notes:
Complements cf.check, which reads a construction file's structure and deliberately never asks whether the chemistry works. Resolution is project-wide because a construction file's inputs live wherever they were made — SynThera's pGhost16 takes one template from SLIP4 and another from SLIP3 — and because some sequences exist only in a labsheet workbook and in no ordering sheet at all. --primes answers the question that follows every simulated PCR and had no tool: a primer with two binding sites gives an unreadable trace and nothing structural can see it. On an annealing failure it measures each primer's longest 3'-anchored exact match against simCF's 18 nt rule, because a mutagenic primer whose designed base falls inside that window is rejected by the simulator and still works at the bench.

--maps answers the question this record has advertised since it was written and could not perform: the product sequences were stripped from --json before anything could compare them, so "does the simulated plasmid match the recorded map" had to be done by hand in an editor. Equal lengths are not an answer — pP6 simulates to 3555 bp and its map is 3555 bp, on the other strand. A plasmid has no first base and no canonical strand, so the comparison is up to rotation AND reverse complement; anything stricter calls a correct construction wrong. THE THIRD OUTCOME IS THE ONE TO READ CAREFULLY: 'no map' means nobody recorded one, which is not agreement, and it is printed for every such product rather than skipped, because a check that quietly passes over what it could not verify reads afterwards as a check that passed. A library product is reported 'no map' too: its skeleton carries N at every slot and cannot be compared base for base.

examples.output:
Construction of pMatch.txt  (project maps)
     pMatch            496 bp

  against the recorded maps:
     pMatch         match      496 bp, reverse complement as pMatch.seq

Construction of pDiff.txt  (project maps)
     pDiff             496 bp

  against the recorded maps:
     pDiff          DIFFERS    simulated 496 bp vs 499 bp in pDiff.seq (-3 bp)
                    first difference at base 201: simulated A, map T
